title: Resolve retained terminal recipe responses
platforms: Linux / Xvfb isolated EUR interpreter; Windows GNU / Wine synthetic tests
changes: Allow explicit recovery of a pending recipe step when its retained successful terminal response exactly matches the original run, request, deadline, operation, session and request fingerprint; record it without dispatching the action again.
Preserve assertions and terminal completion, require a separate explicit recovery to continue remaining steps, and refuse missing, mismatched, failed or wait-attached pending responses.
validation: Linux synthetic regression passed 39 recipe, 36 control, 4 completion, 4 registry and 1 selection test; Windows GNU/Wine passed 39, 37, 4, 4 and 1 respectively.

An isolated Linux/Xvfb run stopped its own client after the server wrote a terminal status response but before the pending checkpoint changed. After a normal reopen, recovery recorded the exact response without redispatch, then resumed one frame; a second resume changed neither checkpoint nor guest state. Protected inputs stayed unchanged.
limitations: The response is trusted local session evidence, not a signed record. Overwritten or unavailable responses and pending actions with attached waits remain refused. The real proof used an intentionally interrupted client and silent audio; real Wine restart, native Windows and physical input remain open.
